requirementChecks.criteria: Deliver exactly the 6 named independent items for tier 6. Duplicate exports do not add items. Only six final static artworks are commissioned; no process, video or presentation is required.
Use the explicitly marked final version; if none is marked, use the last exported version.
Each static role is a separate complete export. Multi-view technical boards are allowed where commissioned; do not count one contact sheet or duplicate export as several roles.

Each image has a readable title beginning with COMMONHOUR and followed by its correct role or state. Placement and typography may vary; a missing title, incorrect state, misspelling or project name appearing only in unrelated body text fails.
The cover identifies COMMONHOUR followed by the materials and connections role. An interior-only project name or a cover naming another role fails.

Read the inventory, dimensions and allocations across the drawings: exactly one each of L, K, M, N, F and C is retained. Stored envelopes are respectively 330 × 230 × 20, 280 × 120 × 20, 120 × 70 × 40, 210 × 297 × 18, 320 × 240 × 40 and 180 × 120 × 70 mm. W shows L open with its 330 × 230 mm base and nominal 220 mm screen rise, K/M/N on the surface, and F/C inside; D and S conceal all six in actual compartments. Rotation and explanatory cutaways are allowed. Shrinking, merging, duplicating or omitting objects, incompatible allocated volumes, or storing L open fails; loose cables remain contained in C.

Dimensioned furniture views establish one table with unchanged assembly identities and totals in all three states. W has at least 1000 × 600 mm of clear working surface; D has at least 1200 × 800 mm and two distinct 600 × 400 mm setting areas; both surfaces are 720–760 mm high. S remains assembled and its entire envelope, including handles, supports and stored kit, is no larger than 1100 × 600 × 850 mm. Expansion mechanism and silhouette may vary. Missing dimensions, contradictory geometry, changed part counts or exceeding any bound fails.

Room insets and the S1 starting view agree with the client coordinate records: room x=0–3600, y=0–3000, z=0–2600; entrance strip y=0–900; solid cabinet x=0–1200, y=2600–3000, z=0–700; window at x=3600, y=1400–2600, z=900–2100; protected floor band x=3300–3600, y=1400–2600; chair parking x=0–1100, y=1000–1550. Retain the existing building and freestanding installation. CH-A and CH-B are the two existing 500 × 500 × 820 mm chairs with 450 mm seats: only CH-A is active in W, both are active in D, and both are parked in S with the table outside parking. Each active chair has a 600 × 900 mm use envelope measured outward from its table edge, outside the entrance strip and window band, with support-free leg space. D includes two 240 mm plates and two 80 × 100 mm cups within the setting areas. Camera and drawing scale may vary; displaced fixed geometry, obstructed protected areas, chair substitution or unusable seating fails. Identified carried parts and people may traverse the circulation strip during movement.

A readable forward sequence connects the delivered W and D assemblies, tracks every component by stable ID, keeps removed pieces and work objects in the room, and assigns final locations. L visibly closes before insertion; L/K/M/N enter dimensioned compartments while F/C are already inside. Compartment allocations and access paths accommodate the recorded object envelopes without interference. The fixed conversion phrase is readable. Different mechanisms and step counts are allowed; unexplained disappearing parts, missing objects, inaccessible storage or a sequence incompatible with the state drawings fails.

The two-page sheet records assembly IDs, grouped fastener counts, quantities and dimensions matching the furniture drawings. Tabletop, storage and tray panels are 18 mm birch plywood with clear water-based lacquer; supports are powder-coated steel tube. Record the chosen powder-coat color, tube section and wall thickness, grips and transformation hardware, plus the selected quantity of M6 relocation bolts with captive nuts and the 4 mm hex key. At least two meaningful joint details explain the actual transformation and separation/reassembly functions, including movement, load support and retention. Shared hardware is allowed when both functions are explained; generic unrelated details, omitted selections or contradictory inventories fail.

Start from the delivered S1 location and account for every separated furniture module, one identified hardware pouch and all six work objects packed together in the 400 × 320 × 180 mm tote. Dimension each module, including protrusions, within 1300 × 850 × 250 mm in its chosen packing orientation, and show two adults' holding/support positions. Trace the contents through the level doorway at y=0, x=200–1000, clear 800 × 2050 mm; preserve its hinge at x=200 and inward 800 mm radius sweep; continue through x=200–1100, y=-900–0 and then rightward through x=1100–3100, y=-900–0 with 2300 mm corridor headroom. Flat, tilted or upright handling is allowed when stated and spatially feasible. Missing contents, omitted turning stages, collisions, unsupported handling or moving the existing chairs/cabinet as part of this sequence fails.

The state drawings, conversion and relocation describe one table with stable assembly identities, quantities, dimensions and actual connections. Work objects retain their identities and counts as they move from W to concealed D/S storage and then into the relocation tote. Room placement, chair states and the relocation start agree with the fixed client coordinates and protected areas.
